pezzi.6: Consulting, training, security hardening and custom-built agent systems. Four ways of working together, always starting from your real case.
pezzi.35: I teach you how, or I build it with you
pezzi.36: Four ways of working together, from a single meeting to a system that is built and maintained. Always on your case, never on textbook examples.
pezzi.38: The difference between the four is not how long they last: it is who keeps a hand on the system at the end.
pezzi.40: One or more sessions to decide: whether an agent is needed, where it is worth putting one, what should be left to a person. I come out with a written scope, not with a generic quote.
pezzi.42: I teach how to build agents: how operations are declared, how they are connected to the data, how what they say is verified. On real tools, with your own case in hand.
pezzi.44: I take a system that is already running and I close it down: permissions in the database, execution isolation, tests that the restriction holds even when the model tries to work around it.
pezzi.46: I design and build the system, for one person or for a company: on the goals you have, on the data you have, inside the security boundaries that are needed.
pezzi.48: The same order, whether it is a single session or an entire system. The scope before the code, the verification before the delivery.
pezzi.50: We work out the goal and the work that is done by hand today
pezzi.52: We write the scope: what the agent can do, what it must not be able to do
pezzi.54: We build: declared operations, permissions, checks
pezzi.56: We try to break it, before someone else does
pezzi.58: Maintenance: periodic checks and updates when the numbers move
pezzi.60: Two different starting points, two different paths. The first question I ask is always the same: what is the work you do by hand today.
pezzi.61: If you are starting from scratch
pezzi.62: What an agent is and what it is not
pezzi.63: How it connects to data and programs already in use
pezzi.64: How to recognise a verifiable result
pezzi.65: What should be automated and what should not
pezzi.66: If you already have something running
pezzi.68: Why the system answers well in a test and badly in service
pezzi.69: How to put a check between whoever executes and whoever approves
pezzi.70: How to move from a cloud model to a local one, and when it is worth it
pezzi.72: I do not teach how to write better instructions. I teach how to build boundaries.
pezzi.74: I do not promise results before I have seen the data and the process: the cost and the time depend on the scope, and the scope is written together. If after the first meeting the answer is that an agent is not needed, I say so.
pezzi.77: Tell me about the work you do by hand today.
